description: OAuth callback state query param reaches res.redirect on the error path, where the getSafeRedirectUrl guard applied on the success path at L120 is omitted, so an off-site target is redirected to.
demotionReason: Mitigation is functionally sound but scope-limited, so the truth table's functional-but-limited row applies. getSafeRedirectUrl covers the success path at packages/app-store/larkcalendar/api/callback.ts:120, and returnTo only survives decodeOAuthState's constant-time nonce HMAC at packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:26-32, which is keyed on NEXTAUTH_SECRET and the victim's own session userId, so a third party cannot mint the state that carries the hostile returnTo. Severity medium, therefore advisory.

description: subscriberUrl accepted by POST /api/webhooks with its URL check commented out is fetched server-side here with no private-range filter, deny-list or DNS-rebinding check, reaching internal hosts.
demotionReason: No demotion; recorded to explain the exposure. Mitigation status is None on the v1 REST path: apps/api/v1/pages/api/webhooks/_post.ts:75 parses the body with schemaWebhookCreateBodyParams, whose subscriberUrl check is commented out at apps/api/v1/lib/validations/webhook.ts:18 and which applies no SSRF refinement, so a plain non-admin API key can register an internal target. The other two write paths do validate - packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/webhook/create.handler.ts:28 and apps/api/v2/src/modules/webhooks/utils/validate-webhook-url.ts:5 - but both use the sync validator that self-documents no DNS-rebinding protection at packages/lib/ssrfProtection.ts:193-196, and the async variant swallows DNS failures at packages/lib/ssrfProtection.ts:185-187, so even the guarded paths are time-of-check-to-time-of-use exposed. All four rule-1 criteria hold.

description: The unvalidated Content-Type request header read at L31 is interpolated into a log.error record that ships to the remote log platform and Sentry, letting any caller pollute or forge log fields.
demotionReason: Mitigation is functionally sound but incomplete, so the functional-but-limited row applies. Node's HTTP header parser rejects raw CR and LF in a header value, so log-entry splitting is not reachable and only field pollution is; mitigation-inventory.txt lists no sanitising wrapper for apps/web/app/api/parseRequestData.ts; and the handler aborts with HttpError 415 at apps/web/app/api/parseRequestData.ts:50 immediately after logging, so the tainted value never reaches an authorization or persistence path. Severity medium, therefore advisory.

description: Feishu twin of the same unauthenticated webhook compares attacker-supplied req.body.token to the stored token with ===, then persists the attacker's app_ticket into the shared credential record.
demotionReason: No demotion; broken-mitigation row on a high-severity sink, reported separately because this is a distinct deployed endpoint. Bypass: the comparison at packages/app-store/feishucalendar/api/events.ts:66 is non-constant-time, feishuKeysSchema at packages/app-store/feishucalendar/api/events.ts:15 declares open_verification_token as z.string() with no .min(1) while packages/app-store/feishucalendar/lib/AppAccessToken.ts:38 uses .min(1), and the route has no auth middleware - mitigation-inventory.txt lists only schema-validation lines for this file. The matched branch writes the attacker-supplied app_ticket into the app keys record, so impact is deployment-wide credential poisoning of the integration.

description: Unauthenticated Lark webhook decides trust by comparing attacker-supplied req.body.token to the stored token with ===; the sibling branch then writes an attacker app_ticket into the shared app keys.
demotionReason: No demotion; this is the truth table's broken-mitigation row on a high-severity sink. Bypass: the comparison at packages/app-store/larkcalendar/api/events.ts:59 is non-constant-time, the named weak mechanism, and larkKeysSchema at packages/app-store/larkcalendar/api/events.ts:15 declares open_verification_token as z.string() with no .min(1), whereas the strict siblings at packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/AppAccessToken.ts:38 use .min(1) and packages/app-store/larkcalendar/zod.ts validates the misspelled key open_verfication_token, so the admin form never enforces non-empty on the key this route reads and an empty stored token authenticates any request that sends an empty token. The route carries no auth middleware - mitigation-inventory.txt lists only schema-validation lines for this file. Impact is deployment-wide because the L66 branch persists the attacker's app_ticket through prisma.app.update at packages/app-store/larkcalendar/api/events.ts:73-81.

description: randomString draws every character from Math.random, a non-cryptographic PRNG, so identifiers built from it are predictable from observed output; it is consumed for OAuth username slugs.
demotionReason: Demoted because no user-controlled source reaches this sink and no secret depends on it, so rule-1 criterion (1) is unmet. The only production consumer is the username slug at packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:104, while every security-bearing value uses node:crypto - randomBytes(32) at packages/features/auth/lib/verifyEmail.ts:37 and :130, and crypto.randomBytes at packages/lib/crypto.ts:17 and packages/lib/crypto/keyring.ts:86. Severity low, therefore advisory.

description: The OAuth callback state query param is JSON.parsed and annotated as IntegrationOAuthCallbackState with no schema check, so any JSON type reaches consumers that treat returnTo as a string.
demotionReason: Mitigation exists and is functionally sound but scope-limited, so the functional-but-limited row applies. The constant-time nonce HMAC at packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:26-32 discards any state a third party did not obtain for the victim's own session, so shape confusion is reachable only with the caller's own state - except for the five NONCE_EXEMPT_APPS declared at packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:6 and short-circuited at L14-16, which return the unvalidated object. AGENTS.md forbids unchecked type assertions, so this is reported as a standards breach as well. Severity medium, therefore advisory.

description: The cron route takes its apiKey from the ?apiKey= query string at L17 and, on a plain !== match, runs an unscoped booking.findMany returning every tenant's pending bookings with attendee PII.
demotionReason: No demotion; broken-mitigation row on a high-severity sink. Bypass: the only authorization is the non-constant-time compare at apps/web/app/api/cron/bookingReminder/route.ts:19, the truth table's named weak mechanism, and L17 also accepts the shared secret in the URL query string, so it leaks into access, proxy and referrer logs and into browser history. mitigation-inventory.txt contains zero auth-middleware, rate-limiting and schema-validation lines anywhere under apps/web/app/api/cron/, and the query at L27 carries no tenant predicate, so nothing bounds the read to one organisation. Judged against the resource.action model documented in PERMISSIONS.md, no permission check is performed at all.

description: A routing-form owner's stored message and errorMessage are rendered through dangerouslySetInnerHTML on a public page, so any sanitizer gap becomes stored XSS against every visitor of that form.
demotionReason: Mitigation is functionally sound but its ordering is weak, which keeps this advisory rather than a gate-block. packages/lib/markdownToSafeHTML.ts:16 runs sanitize-html over the rendered markdown, yet four regex rewrites at packages/lib/markdownToSafeHTML.ts:18-34 re-emit HTML after sanitisation, so the sanitizer is no longer the last transformation applied. Each rewrite only reorders or annotates output the sanitizer already escaped and no bypass payload was demonstrated. Severity medium, therefore advisory.

description: The JSON parse error, which embeds a snippet of the attacker's request body, is interpolated with req.nextUrl into a logger call, placing attacker-controlled text where a format template is consumed.
demotionReason: Demoted because the mechanism is not reachable: the template is fully materialised into one string argument before log.error is invoked at apps/web/app/api/parseRequestData.ts:36, so no trailing argument exists for a %s, %o or %j specifier to consume. The only inventoried multi-argument candidates interpolate an internal enum - packages/features/booking-audit/lib/service/BookingAuditTaskerProducerService.ts:109 and :136 - and the two performance.measure calls at apps/web/app/api/defaultResponderForAppDir.ts:76 and packages/lib/server/defaultResponder.ts:77 perform no printf formatting at all. Severity low, therefore advisory.

description: Every v1 API route dispatches through a bracket lookup keyed by the attacker-chosen HTTP method under an unchecked keyof assertion, so a method outside the declared union indexes the handler map.
demotionReason: Mitigation exists and is functionally sound: the truthiness guard at packages/lib/server/defaultHandler.ts:11-15 returns 405 whenever the lookup yields no handler, and inherited members such as constructor or toString expose no .default property, so the optional chain resolves to undefined rather than to a callable. Node's HTTP parser additionally restricts the method to a known token set. The unchecked assertion is still reported because AGENTS.md forbids it. Severity low, therefore advisory.

description: A filesystem write sink persists freshly generated secret material to a workspace file in plaintext, so any process, image layer or backup with read access to the checkout obtains it.
demotionReason: Demoted because no user-controlled source reaches the sink: the destination is a compile-time constant built from __dirname at apps/api/v2/scripts/generate-secrets.ts:8 with no request-derived component, and the module is a standalone script that no route or controller imports, so it is unreachable in production. Severity low, therefore advisory. The secret value is deliberately not recorded here.

description: All six NextAuth cookies derive Secure, the __Secure- prefix and SameSite from one useSecureCookies flag, so on any deployment whose resolved URL is http the session token is emitted without Secure.
demotionReason: Mitigation is functionally sound but deployment-dependent, so the functional-but-limited row applies. httpOnly is set on the session token at packages/lib/default-cookies.ts:34 and the __Secure- prefix is applied at packages/lib/default-cookies.ts:18 whenever useSecureCookies is true, so a correctly configured HTTPS deployment is unaffected; the exposure requires a plaintext or misreported-scheme deployment. SECURITY.md's out-of-scope list also excludes Secure and HttpOnly omission on non-sensitive cookies, which bounds the rationale without suppressing the finding. Severity medium, therefore advisory.

description: The payment id path parameter is fetched with no ownership predicate and the ownership test runs only afterwards, so the 401 versus 404 split becomes a cross-tenant oracle for which payment ids exist.
demotionReason: Mitigation exists and is functionally sound but scope-limited, so the functional-but-limited row applies. The membership test at apps/api/v1/pages/api/payments/[id].ts:56 blocks payload disclosure and withMiddleware("HTTP_GET") at apps/api/v1/pages/api/payments/[id].ts:70 enforces API-key authentication, so no other tenant's payment body is returned. It does not remove the existence oracle, because the 401 at L57 and the not-found catch at L62-67 are observably different, and the catch also serialises the raw error object into the response body. Severity medium, therefore advisory.

description: A booking id path parameter drives a findUnique that includes every column of the related user, attendees and payment rows, materialising two-factor and payment fields far beyond what is returned.
demotionReason: Mitigation exists and is functionally sound but limited to the response boundary, so the functional-but-limited row applies. Authorization runs before dispatch - apps/api/v1/pages/api/bookings/[id]/index.ts:12 invokes the middleware, which throws 403 at apps/api/v1/pages/api/bookings/[id]/_auth-middleware.ts:91-92 - and the payload is narrowed by schemaBookingReadPublic.parse at apps/api/v1/pages/api/bookings/[id]/_get.ts:119. The over-selected columns still reach error and log serialisation, and the three @calcom/eslint/no-prisma-include-true suppressions at L105, L107 and L109 are dead after the migration to Biome, so the select-over-include standard in AGENTS.md now has no automated enforcement. Severity medium, therefore advisory.

description: Authorising a single payment loads the caller's entire booking set with include bookings true, so every column of every booking is materialised purely to run an id membership test.
demotionReason: Demoted because the over-selected rows belong to the caller: the query is keyed on the session-derived userId at apps/api/v1/pages/api/payments/[id].ts:48 and withMiddleware("HTTP_GET") at apps/api/v1/pages/api/payments/[id].ts:70 authenticates the caller, so no cross-tenant data is read. The exposure is confined to error and log serialisation paths. The @calcom/eslint/no-prisma-include-true suppression at L49 is dead after the migration to Biome. Severity low, therefore advisory.

description: Existing reminders are read at L83 and filtered at L95, the organiser email is sent at L144, and only then is the reminderMail row created, so concurrent runs both pass the check and send duplicates.
demotionReason: Mitigation is a broken mechanism but severity is medium, so the truth table's broken row yields an advisory rather than a gate-block. The only gate is the non-constant-time CRON_API_KEY compare at apps/web/app/api/cron/bookingReminder/route.ts:19, and no transaction, row lock or unique constraint spans the L83 read and the L146 write - contrast the SELECT FOR UPDATE lock the booking path takes at packages/features/bookings/lib/handleSeats/create/createNewSeat.ts:53. Impact is bounded to duplicate outbound reminder email with no data corruption, and SECURITY.md's out-of-scope list treats denial-of-service style amplification as out of bounty scope, which bounds severity without suppressing the finding.

description: The OAuth code query parameter is exchanged for tokens and the credential is persisted at L65 without checking which scopes Google actually granted, so a downscoped grant is stored as complete.
demotionReason: Mitigation exists and is functionally sound but scope-limited, so the functional-but-limited row applies. The route requires a session at apps/web/app/api/teams/googleworkspace/callback/route.ts:30, schema-validates the state at L40 and requires team-admin authority at L43 via throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam, so rule-1 criterion (4) fails - it is not exploitable without admin access to the team. The granted-scope check that packages/app-store/googlecalendar/api/callback.ts:55-57 performs against GOOGLE_CALENDAR_SCOPES is simply absent on this route. Severity medium, therefore advisory.

description: The repository's only $executeRawUnsafe call builds an INSERT into the managed-event-type user join table inside a transaction, so any interpolated identifier would execute as attacker-authored SQL.
demotionReason: Demoted because the statement is fully parameterised: connectUsersToEventTypesQueryWithParams at packages/features/ee/managed-event-types/lib/handleChildrenEventTypes.ts:103-135 emits only positional placeholders at L124 and binds server-derived ids as parameters at L127-128, so no request value ever reaches the SQL text. Sink-inventory category 17 also contains zero eval, new Function and vm.runIn call sites - every other hit is an identifier whose name ends in Function( or a setTimeout given a function reference - and only one of the 305 raw-query lines uses an Unsafe variant at all. Severity low, therefore advisory.

description: The unauthenticated BTCPay webhook body is JSON.parsed and drives a payment lookup and credential decode before the HMAC is verified, letting a caller probe invoice ids and payment state pre-auth.
demotionReason: Mitigation exists and is functionally sound but is applied late, so the functional-but-limited row applies. The payload is schema-checked immediately by btcpayWebhookSchema.safeParse at packages/app-store/btcpayserver/api/webhook.ts:54 and the signature is verified in constant time by crypto.timingSafeEqual at packages/app-store/btcpayserver/api/webhook.ts:85-88, guarded by the length pre-check at L82, so no unsigned payload can settle a payment. The residual exposure is ordering only: the repository lookup at L62 and the credential parse at L68-71 precede verification and the 404, 200 and 400 branches are observably different. Severity medium, therefore advisory.

description: The rich-text editor deserialises an untrusted workflow or event-type template into DOM nodes in the browser, so an XML parser on this path would resolve entities the template author declares.
demotionReason: Demoted because no XML parser is instantiated: both calls parse with mimeType text/html - packages/ui/components/editor/plugins/ToolbarPlugin.tsx:373 and :395 - and the browser DOMParser never resolves external entities or fetches a DTD in HTML mode. Sink-inventory category 19 contains only these two lines and no xml2js, libxmljs or SAXParser call site anywhere in the non-test tree. Severity low, therefore advisory.
